         3                  THE SECRETARY:    By Senator

         4       Oppenheimer, Legislative Resolution Number

         5       768, memorializing Governor David A. Paterson

         6       to proclaim March 2009 as Women's History

         7       Month in the State of New York.

         8                  ACTING SENATOR BRESLIN:    Senator

         9       Oppenheimer.

        10                  SENATOR OPPENHEIMER:    Thank you

        11       very much.

        12                  I'd like to just speak very briefly

        13       on this resolution, which is an important

        14       resolution for recognition of what women have

        15       done governmentally in this state.

        16                  Each year New York State does set

        17       aside time to recognize the unique and varied

        18       contributions that women have made to New York

        19       and to New York society.  And New York has

        20       been the home of many extraordinary women who

        21       have led society to a better place, as many

        22       men will attest to.

        23                  New York has had people working and

        24       living in New York like Susan B. Anthony, like

 

                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                        1217

 

         1       Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Matilda Joslyn

         2       Gage.  They were all very active in our

         3       struggle for suffrage.  And indeed, in the

         4       late 1800s, Carrie Clyde Holly, who was

         5       originally from New York City, and Clara

         6       Dressingham, who came from Brooklyn, were

         7       among two of the first three women elected to

         8       any state legislature in the nation, joining

         9       Frances Klock, from Massachusetts, in the

        10       Colorado legislature.

        11                  And in 1918, one year after

        12       New York guaranteed women the right to vote in

        13       all elections, the first two women, Ida Sammis

        14       and Mary Lilly, were elected to the New York

        15       State Legislature.

        16                  And there are many other women that

        17       have been very active in New York State

        18       government.  For example, Rhoda Fox Graves

        19       became the first woman to be elected to both

        20       houses of the New York State government,

        21       elected to the Assembly in 1924, for several

        22       terms, and then elected to the Senate in 1934.

        23       And she was here for 14 years in this house.

        24                  And then we have Rhoda Jacobs, our

 

                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                        1218

 

         1       friend.  She's the longest-serving woman in

         2       the New York State Legislature, from 1979.

         3       And Rhoda is still here presently and working

         4       hard.

         5                  And Earlene Hooper, who is the

         6       highest-ranking woman in the Assembly.  And as

         7       Deputy Speaker, she holds the highest

         8       leadership post ever held by a woman in the

         9       Assembly.  And Ruth Hassell-Thompson, of note,

        10       is the highest-ranking woman in the Senate, as

        11       Chair of our Majority Conference, which we are

        12       all very pleased with.

        13                  And since 1983, the New York women

        14       legislators have worked through the bipartisan

        15       Legislative Women's Caucus to improve the

        16       representation and participation of all women

        17       in all areas of government, to support issues

        18       that affect women and families in New York

        19       State, and to provide a network of support for

        20       the women in the State Legislature.

        21                  And today we have 52 women serving

        22       in the New York State Legislature, holding

        23       leadership positions in both houses and

        24       bringing the diverse experience of women into

         5       State of New York and to honor the women of

         6       New York State.  And we hope this will be

         9       Women's Legislative Caucus is bicameral and

        10       also bipartisan.  And we are 52 women, and we

        11       are working to advance those family issues so
